title: Annotatio II §.V: Bellarmine — conversion/transubstantiation propagator; Cave seconds; Rhadebert’s own sayings
pass_a_gloss: Much more rightly held by Bellarmine to be a Propagator of Conversion, the rudiment of Transubstantiation — both in the Controversies Tom. on the Eucharist p. m. 579 and in the book On Ecclesiastical Writers p. 150 — our most celebrated countryman William Cave approving the same and adding his vote (Literary History of Ecclesiastical Writers p. 376), this part being propped by Paschasius’s own very many utterances in On the body and blood of the Lord ch. 20.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine is nearer the mark: Paschasius propagates Conversion, the seed of Transubstantiation (Eucharist Controversies; Ecclesiastical Writers).
Cave adds his vote; Paschasius’s own On the body and blood of the Lord ch. 20 props that reading.
source_text: Rectiùs multo à Bellarmino Conversionis, Transsubstantiationis rudimenti, Propagatorem habitum, cùm Tom. Controv. de Eucharist. p. m. 579. tùm in libro de Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis p. 150., probante idem calculumque adjiciente suum Nostrate Viro Celeberrimo Wilhelmo Caveô, Script. Eccles. Hist. literaria p. 376., suffulciendo hac in parte ipsis Rhadeberti enunciatis quàm plurimis in libro de corpore & sanguine Domini cap. 20.
